q-37362.name: Question 1
q-37362.problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $N$ given that 

$$
N[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-37362.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), right-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $N:$

$$
N={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore, $N$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $N$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P:$

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$

Question 1
?

Find the eigenvectors of the 2×2 matrix N given that N[2112]=[2112][500−1].

a
[50] and [0−1]
b
[22] and [11]
c
[−21] and [1−2]
d
[21] and [12]
e
[12] and [12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the matrix [2112] appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), right-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for N:

N=[2112]⏟P[500−1]⏟D[2112]−1⏟P−1

Therefore, N is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of N are λ1=5 and λ2=−1 and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix P:

v1=[21] and v2=[12]

q-86682.name: Question 2
q-86682.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $A:$

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $A=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${A}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{A}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{71} & =P{D}^{71}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{71}(\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}(-1)^{71} & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{71}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-86693.problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-86693.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $B:$ 

$$
B={{{[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore, $B$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $B$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=7$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}]$

q-86694.problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]T=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-86694.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $T:$

$$
T={{{[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore, $T$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $T$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-4$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 3 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$

T=[7532]−1⏟P[500−4]⏟D[7532]⏟P−1

Therefore, T is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of T are λ1=5 and λ2=−4 and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix P. Computing P, we obtain

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are:

v1=[−23] and v2=[5−7]

$$

Since $C=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${C}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{C}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
